This entry-level AI Engineer will work under close supervision to apply developing technical knowledge in Software Engineering and Generative AI, performing analytic, testing, modeling, and development tasks on smaller projects, and independently on larger, more complex assignments. Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, documents methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Support development of AI-enabled applications and fix straightforward defects under close supervision.
Build and maintain components of LLM-based solutions, including API integrations, prompt and tool/function-calling workflows, and basic RAG pipelines (chunking, embeddings, vector search).
Clean, transform, and analyze data with Python, SQL, and data libraries; build simple ETL steps and visualizations.
Execute assigned test cases, including unit tests and basic retrieval or model evaluations, and help reproduce reported issues.
Serve models and AI services through RESTAPIs and containers, prepare simple configuration changes, and follow deployment runbooks.
Track experiments and model versions and support monitoring and CI/CD processes.
Document work and escalation steps in tickets and knowledge base entries.
Learn codebase, development workflows, and platform fundamentals through pairing and code reviews.

Databases SQL (essential): SELECT, WHERE, JOINs, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, indexes, query optimization
Relational databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite; schema design, normalization, primary and foreign keys, transactions
Python connectivity: SQLAlchemy, psycopg2, pandas.read_sql
NoSQL: MongoDB (documents), Redis (caching)
Vector databases (AI-specific): embeddings, similarity search, and tools such as pgvector, Chroma, FAISS, Pinecone
Data pipelines: ETL basics, data warehouses, Airflow concepts
Modern GenAI Skills LLM APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, structured outputs, tool/function calling
RAG: chunking, embeddings, vector search, retrieval evaluation
Frameworks: LangChain or LlamaIndex (know the basics, but understand what's underneath)
Agents: tool use, multi-step workflows, basic evaluation, and guardrails
MLOps and Deployment Model serving: FastAPI, Docker
Experiment tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases
Cloud basics: AWS, Azure, or GCP
CI/CD basics, monitoring, model versioning

Position Description:
For the Associate Scientist II position, we are seeking a highly motivated candidate who can independently generate precise, reliable and reproducible data in a timely manner. Can demonstrate experimental precision and strong data interpretation skills. They should possess understanding of core discipline and support early phase development of New Chemical Entities (NCEs) drug substance and drug product in both preclinical and clinical programs. Collaborate within the global Analytical R&D organization and with R&D cross-functional partners such as Pre-Clinical Safety (PCS), Process Chemistry, Process Engineering, Drug Product Development (DPD), and Quality Assurance (QA) and CMC-Regulatory.
Responsibilities:
Independently plan and perform routine tasks competently within a timely fashion and generate precise, reliable and consistent results.
Demonstrate experimental precision and strong data interpretation skills and should possess understanding of core discipline.
Documentation of experimental activities and results in a GMP compliant fashion using an electronic data acquisition and management systems.
Analyze and critique results, noting significant deviations from the expected results.
Troubleshoot experiments and instrumentation.
Learn and understand new experimental techniques with a curiosity to apply them for unique project / assignment requirements.
Demonstrate skill in multiple techniques and appropriately modify protocols, as required, to suit the changing needs of research or development sciences.
Place data in proper scientific context by consulting and citing relevant literature.
Demonstrate technical proficiency in their field, preferentially in the analytical areas of quantitative and instrumental analysis.
Raises the bar and is never satisfied with the status quo.
Impact projects predominantly through lab and/or pilot plant based activities.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, or equivalent education, with typically 3 or more years’ experience or Master’s Degree or equivalent education (no additional experience).
Theoretical and practical knowledge (in chromatography and / or spectroscopy is highly preferred) to carry out job function.
Builds strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Learns fast, grasps the "essence" and can change course quickly where indicated.
Creates a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement.
Embraces the ideas of others, nurtures innovation, and manages innovation to reality.
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

As the Manager, Sales Incentive Compensation, Immunology, you’ll play a key role in developing and managing motivational sales incentive programs across the Immunology organization that are aligned to each business’s strategic objectives. You’ll be responsible for all aspects of IC, from base program design, fairness and equity testing, and pay curve evaluation to SPIFF modeling and implementation, as well as field communication, education, and support. Consulting:
Plan, design, analyze, implement, communicate, administer, and validate all sales incentive programs, including contests and kickers.
Develop incentive programs based on identified marketing and commercial strategies, available resources, and overarching incentive program design.
Provide guidance and support in the development of special incentives; assess special incentive requests against business needs and guiding principles, and evaluate proposals for data availability and cost/time requirements.
Manage and work closely with the compensation processing vendor on project management, incentive validation, change implementation, and reporting, ensuring upcoming franchise-specific changes are communicated to the vendor team in a timely manner.
Collaborate with Sales, Sales Management, Marketing, Marketing Analytics and Business Insights, Forecasting, Sales Reporting, and Executive Leadership to ensure programs are fair, equitable, motivating, valid, and aligned with corporate objectives.

PhD with 5+ years of experience in area or scientific area of discipline. Demonstrated depth in computational engineering, with several years of applied, industrially relevant experience in multi-physics simulation and a proven record of translating simulation results into design, process, or manufacturing decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading a small team of engineers with strong modeling competence, including delegation of meaningful ownership, technical coaching, performance feedback, and accountability for team deliverables.

description:

Position Summary
The Senior Principal Engineer, Mechanical is an established subject-matter expert who works with little to no supervision and provides technical leadership for utility, process and sanitary piping, pressure vessels, tanks, heat exchangers, fabricated equipment, materials of construction, welding, and mechanical integrity across AbbVie manufacturing, laboratory, research, and infrastructure investments. The role leads complex technical workstreams from front-end planning through detailed design, fabrication, construction, commissioning, qualification, startup, and lifecycle support.
This is an individual-contributor role with broad technical influence. The engineer directs technical work through project teams, engineering partners, fabricators, and suppliers; provides guidance to less-experienced engineers; and is frequently consulted to resolve complex or ambiguous mechanical engineering, code-compliance, fabrication, and field issues. Technical outputs must support patient and employee safety, product quality, regulatory compliance, hygienic design, reliability, maintainability, sustainability, schedule, and lifecycle value.
Key Responsibilities
Lead mechanical engineering workstreams for complex brownfield and greenfield capital projects and programs, including discipline planning, scope definition, deliverable development, technical resource coordination, schedule integration, and management of discipline budgets and engineering hours.
Define and approve mechanical design criteria, system philosophies, Basis of Design documents, specifications, datasheets, equipment and piping classes, materials requirements, fabrication requirements, inspection plans, and commissioning strategies.
Provide technical leadership for utility, process and sanitary piping, pressure vessels, storage and process tanks, heat exchangers, coils, mixers, jacketed systems, skids and superskids, specialty nozzles, valves, supports, and associated mechanical interfaces.
Lead review of pipe-routing and space planning, maintainability reviews, modularization strategies, equipment arrangement, 3D model reviews, and constructability assessments, including evaluation of automated versus manual welding approaches for shop-fabricated skids.
Perform or independently verify mechanical calculations and analyses, including pressure design, minimum wall thickness, MAWP, nozzle and external loads, thermal expansion, pipe stress, equipment support loads, heat-transfer duty, relief and design-condition interfaces, and fatigue or fitness-for-service evaluations as applicable.
Review and approve P&IDs, piping plans, isometrics, orthographic and fabrication drawings, vessel and exchanger drawings, equipment layouts, support details, weld maps, material certificates, stress-analysis reports, inspection records, NDE documentation, deviations, and turnover packages.
Apply and interpret applicable requirements, including ASME BPVC Section VIII, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, ASME BPE, TEMA, API 579/ASME FFS-1, API tank practices, NFPA requirements, Pressure Equipment Directive requirements, and jurisdictional boiler and pressure-vessel regulations.
Integrate hygienic and mechanical design requirements, including product-contact materials, surface finish, drainability, dead-leg control, cleanability, CIP/SIP geometry, sanitary fittings, weld quality, material traceability, elastomer and gasket selection, and prevention of contamination or corrosion.
Support HAZOPs, HAZIDs, process hazard reviews, mechanical-integrity reviews, management-of-change evaluations, constructability reviews, incident or failure investigations, and resolution of discipline-related safety findings and risk-reduction actions.
Provide technical recommendations for mechanical integrity, corrosion prevention, equipment life extension, repair, alteration, rerating, fitness-for-service, failure analysis, and code compliance. Support Operations and Maintenance in resolving complex field conditions and recurring reliability issues.
Advise project and site leadership on technical alternatives, code requirements, quality risks, supplier capability, cost and schedule impacts, standardization opportunities, and operational readiness. Escalate issues with clear evidence and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate with Project Management, Site Engineering, Operations, Maintenance, Quality, Validation/CQV, EHS, MS&T, Process Engineering, Automation, Civil/Structural, Electrical, Procurement, and external engineering partners to ensure complete, coordinated, constructible, and operable solutions.
Develop construction, commissioning, and startup strategy development and provide critical support for technical query and RFI resolution, submittal review, field walkdowns, weld and installation issue resolution, punch-list development, pressure and leak testing review, pre-commissioning support, turnover documentation, and verification that installed systems meet design intent.
Manage technical performance of EPCM firms, engineering contractors, fabricators, and equipment suppliers. Review work plans, calculations, specifications, schedules, procedures, inspection and test plans, quality documentation, and vendor data for technical compliance and execution readiness.
Lead supplier technical assessments, critical fabrication audits, shop visits, factory acceptance testing, nonconformance resolution, and technical acceptance recommendations for high-risk or specialized mechanical equipment and fabricated systems.
Develop, improve, and promote AbbVie engineering standards, specifications, standard details, design tools, QA/QC practices, and reusable technical guidance. Transfer lessons learned across sites, regions, projects, and supplier networks.
Mentor engineers and designers, provide technical review and coaching, deliver discipline-specific training and workshops, and foster engineering excellence, accountability, collaboration, ethical conduct, and proactive risk management.
Represent the mechanical discipline in governance forums, project reviews, investigations, change controls, CAPAs, supplier-quality reviews, inspection-readiness activities, and external standards or industry forums as assigned.
Decision-Making and Organizational Impact
Independently establishes technical approaches and priorities for assigned complex projects, programs, and mechanical systems within approved governance and business objectives.
Serves as a discipline escalation point for complex technical issues, code interpretations, fabrication deviations, equipment failures, nonconformances, supplier concerns, and field modifications.
Provides expert contributions that materially influence project outcomes, equipment integrity, hygienic performance, compliance, capital deployment, production continuity, and lifecycle operating cost.
Exercises judgment where requirements are incomplete, codes require interpretation, or solutions require integration of technical, quality, safety, operational, procurement, financial, and schedule considerations.
Influences cross-functional teams, sites, contractors, and suppliers without relying on direct reporting authority; decisions may affect multiple projects, facilities, technology platforms, or global standards.
Minimum Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline and typically at least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in process utilities, piping, static equipment, mechanical integrity, facilities engineering, or capital project engineering. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered in accordance with company policy.
Demonstrated experience independently leading complex mechanical engineering scope through multiple project phases in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, food and beverage, chemical, industrial gas, energy, or similarly regulated or process-intensive environments.
Demonstrated working knowledge of pressure vessels, tanks, heat exchangers, process or sanitary piping, materials of construction, fabrication, welding, NDE, inspection, commissioning, and field implementation.
Demonstrated ability to resolve complex technical problems, interpret codes and standards, coordinate multidisciplinary stakeholders, oversee suppliers or engineering partners, and produce clear technical documentation and recommendations.
Ability to read and evaluate P&IDs, piping plans and isometrics, equipment and fabrication drawings, 3D models, mechanical calculations, inspection records, material documentation, and construction work packages.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Welding Engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience with pharmaceutical manufacturing, biologics, aseptic processing, oral solid dose, laboratories, high-purity utilities, cleanrooms, sanitary equipment, and GxP documentation.
Depth in one or more specialty areas: ASME pressure vessels, process or sanitary piping, pipe stress, heat exchangers, tanks, welding engineering, materials and corrosion, hygienic design, mechanical integrity, or fitness-for-service.
Experience with CAESAR II, AutoPIPE, PV Elite, COMPRESS, AutoCAD, Revit, Plant 3D, Navisworks, SolidWorks, or comparable calculation, drafting, and 3D model-review tools.
Credential such as AWS Certified Welding Inspector, National Board Commission, ASNT or ACCP NDT certification, API 510/570/653, Certified Reliability Engineer, or commissioning-related certification.
Core Capabilities
Deep mechanical engineering expertise with strong understanding of system integration, code compliance, hygienic design, fabrication, supplier quality, commissioning, reliability, maintainability, and facility operations.

Work is performed in office, project, laboratory, manufacturing, utility, fabrication-shop, and construction environments. title: Sr Scientist or Scientist, Systems Immunology
location: Cambridge, MA, US
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. AbbVie Immunology is expanding its discovery Systems Immunology team in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The team is focused on identifying new targets for the treatment of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases through computational analysis of human disease tissue-derived datasets and validating targets using humanized experimental approaches.
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled individual to join our team as a Computational Immunology Scientist. The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.
The scientist will work in a multidisciplinary team analyzing multiomics datasets to derive insights into immunological diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets relevant to patient cohorts and AbbVie pipeline drugs. The candidate will also contribute to scientific conference presentations, peer-reviewed publications of translational findings, new drug applications, and regulatory filings. If you are passionate about translating complex biological data into actionable insights and advancing personalized medicine, we encourage you to apply.
This position will be based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and requires passion, attention to detail, prior hands-on experience, and teamwork.
Key Responsibilities:
Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.
Analyze scATAC-seq data to identify differential accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and candidate regulatory programs; integrate accessibility with gene expression to infer peak-to-gene relationships.
Analyze TCR/BCR repertoires, including clonotype assignment, clonal expansion, diversity, V(D)J usage, and sharing across tissues or time points; link clonotypes to matched single-cell profiles.
Analyze bulk RNA-seq and Olink proteomics data and integrate multiomics findings to support target prioritization and biomarker hypotheses; maintain documented, version-controlled workflows and evaluate methods using cloud or high-performance computing.
Collaborate with internal and external scientists to prioritize hypotheses for validation, communicate findings and limitations, and contribute to presentations and publications.
BS, MS, or PhD in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, biostatistics, computer science, or a related quantitative field with typically 5-12 years (BS), 2-10 years (MS), or 0-4 years (PhD) of relevant experience.
Hands-on scRNA-seq analysis experience or experience with scATAC-seq or TCR/BCR analysis, with interest in developing expertise across both.
Proficiency in Python and/or R and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.
Experience with commonly used bioinformatics tools and frameworks such as Scanpy, AnnData, Cell Ranger, scvi-tools, DESeq2, GSEA, WGCNA, or related methods.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, multiple-testing correction, batch effects, and biological replication in high-dimensional datasets.
Ability to translate biological questions into analyses, interpret and communicate results critically, collaborate effectively, and manage multiple priorities with attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality analyses with attention to detail.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience analyzing Olink or other high-plex proteomics datasets.
Experience with CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or integrative multi-omics analysis.
Experience building or benchmarking machine-learning models, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative models, transfer learning, or foundation models.
Experience with cloud or high-performance computing, including AWS and/or SLURM.
Understanding of immunology and inflammatory disease biology; experience supporting target discovery with experimental teams and communicating research through presentations, publications, or reports.
Evidence of scientific communication through presentations, posters, publications, technical reports, or related research contributions.
Position will be filled at level commensurate with extent of education, experience, and accomplishment— Scientist I, Scientist II, Sr Scientist I, or Sr Scientist II

title: Policy Lead, California
location: California, United States
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb's US & Canada Public Policy team represents Airbnb and the interests of our community of hosts and guests before the legislators, regulators, opinion leaders and coalitions who shape the political and legal environment for our business. We operate in heavily regulated spaces in the technology sector: short-term rental rules are written and rewritten at the state, county and municipal level, and the outcomes directly determine where and how Airbnb can grow.
The Difference You Will Make:
The Policy Lead, California holds ultimate responsibility for Airbnb's public policy and regulatory strategy in the state. This is a senior leadership position accountable for three interlocking outcomes:
Business growth. Protecting and expanding Airbnb's ability to operate across California by securing workable regulatory frameworks at the state and local level and defending against measures that would restrict supply or impose restrictive compliance burdens.
Regulatory affairs. Managing an active, high-volume docket of state legislation, local ordinances, administrative rulemaking and enforcement,  ensuring Airbnb's position is well represented in each.
Brand reputation among policymakers. Above all, materially improving how lawmakers, regulators and civic leaders perceive Airbnb and its host community, and converting that credibility into durable policy outcomes.
The role is as much internal as it is external. You will  lead a team of Policy Managers covering California's priority markets, manage a bench of external consultants and lobbyists, and be accountable for the state's annual policy budget. Equally important, the Lead serves as the central point of alignment between Public Policy and the cross-functional partners whose decisions shape our regulatory position: Legal, Supply, Communications, Marketing, Safety, Tax, and the business leadership for the region. Success requires building consensus across these functions on a single integrated strategy and then driving its execution.
The Policy Lead reports to the US and Canada Policy Strategy Director and works in close collaboration with the Head of Public Policy and the broader policy leadership team.
A Typical Day:
Set and own the California strategy:
Develop and own a fully integrated, multi-year state and local public policy strategy for California, grounded in data, political analysis and a clear-eyed assessment of regulatory risk and growth opportunity.
Prioritize across a large and dynamic portfolio of state bills, local ordinances, ballot measures, administrative proceedings, allocating team, consultant and financial resources to the matters that most affect the business.
Define measurable objectives for the state and report progress, risks and outcomes to the Director and senior business leadership on a regular cadence.
Own and manage the California policy budget, including consultant and lobbyist engagements, campaign tactics such as paid media, research, programs and political engagement, ensuring resources are deployed against strategic priorities.
Lead cross-functional alignment:
Serve as Public Policy's primary counterpart to Legal on California matters, partnering on strategy, regulatory interpretation and compliance.
Work with Supply leadership to align regulatory strategy with growth targets, understand the on-the-ground impact of proposed rules, and shape product and operational responses to regulation.
Partner with Communications and Marketing to build and execute reputation strategies directed at policymakers and the civic audiences who influence them, including narrative development, earned and paid media, research publication and third-party validation.
Ensure that internal stakeholders at every level understand the California strategy, that information flows to those who need it, and that roadblocks and wins are surfaced early.
Drive external advocacy and reputation:
Represent Airbnb at the most senior levels of California state and local government, including legislative leadership, the Governor's office, state agencies, mayors, county supervisors and city councils.
Build and sustain a broad network of relationships across legislative, executive and administrative offices, and with the coalitions, trade associations, labor, housing and tourism stakeholders whose positions shape outcomes.
Deploy the full range of advocacy tools available to a regulated marketplace: direct lobbying, coalition campaigns, host and guest mobilization, economic impact research, paid and earned media, political strategy.
Serve as a spokesperson on California policy matters as needed, in coordination with Communications.
Negotiate directly with government counterparts to secure regulatory frameworks that are workable for hosts and consistent with Airbnb's national and global approach.
Build and lead the team:
Lead, coach and develop a team of Policy Managers and the consultants who support them, setting clear objectives, holding the team accountable for results, and investing in their growth as strategists and advocates.
Own recruitment, performance management and succession planning for the California team.
Foster an inclusive, high-performing culture consistent with Airbnb's core values, and create opportunities for team members to lead projects that stretch their strategic and operational skills.
Ensure consultants and lobbyists are properly briefed, aligned to strategy and delivering measurable value.
Your Expertise:
12 to 15+ years of progressively senior experience in public policy, government relations, political campaigns, public affairs or regulatory strategy, in a corporate, consulting, governmental or advocacy setting.
Deep knowledge of California politics and government, including the Legislature, state agencies and major local jurisdictions, and an established network of relationships across them.
Demonstrated success leading strategy in a heavily regulated or politically contested industry; experience in travel, housing, technology platforms or other regulated marketplaces is strongly preferred.
Proven track record of changing how policymakers perceive an organization or issue, and of translating improved reputation into concrete legislative or regulatory outcomes.
Experience leading integrated advocacy campaigns that combine direct lobbying with coalition building, grassroots mobilization, research and paid and earned media.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional alignment at senior levels, build consensus among stakeholders with competing priorities, and drive a shared strategy to execution.
Senior people-leadership experience, including hiring, performance management, coaching and developing a multidisciplinary team; experience managing external consultants and lobbyists.
Strong command of budget planning and resource allocation in a results-driven environment.
Ability to rapidly absorb complex legislative, regulatory and technical material and translate it into clear positions and compelling advocacy.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the credibility to represent Airbnb before senior government officials, the media and internal executives.
Experience on political campaigns, in public relations or public affairs, or in strategic consulting is a strong plus.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in law, public policy or a related field preferred.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join
Our Global Markets Growth & Business Operations team is growing. Our goal is to accelerate growth in our managed countries and to turn each country's ambition into a plan that gets delivered. We work closely with Brand Marketing, Growth Marketing, Product, Communications, Supply, Policy and Finance teams, both central and local, to develop growth levers, streamline operations, and drive impact for countries.
The Difference You Will Make
We are looking for someone to own and scale the growth operations capability for our global markets. You will set the direction for how we identify, pilot and scale new levers that capture growth country by country, and you will hold the organization accountable to deliver. This is a high-visibility role where your influence comes from the quality of your thinking and your ability to mobilize teams across a global matrix.
You will partner with Growth Marketing, Brand Marketing, Finance, Product and country leadership to build playbooks that can be implemented across markets, and you will shape the annual country plans and the central Global Markets strategy, including executive presentations to senior leadership.
This role requires expertise in business operations, marketplace dynamics, marketing channels and implementation, and a strong understanding of supply dynamics.
A Typical Day
Growth strategy and programs
Own the strategy for the growth levers we run across global markets: decide where to invest, what to scale, and what to stop.
Identify, pilot and scale new local demand levers, such as guest incentives and promotions, dynamic merchandising, local partnerships and local marketing, piloting new approaches before building the infrastructure to operate them at scale.
Turn successful pilots into playbooks that countries can adopt, adapting them to local market realities.
Build the investment case for new programs: sizing, business case, and the alignment needed to win resources in global planning cycles.
Country plans and operating rhythm
Lead the development of annual and quarterly country plans and the central Global Markets strategy, setting and pressure-testing targets with country and functional leaders.
Own the operating cadence: business reviews and OKR tracking that give leadership a single, trusted view of performance and the story behind it.
Convert strategy into sequenced execution plans with named owners, milestones and success measures; surface risks early and drive them to resolution.
Track business performance by country and the impact of the current playbook of levers, and act on what you find.
Cross-functional leadership
Act as the connective tissue between country teams and central functions including Growth Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product, Communications, Supply, Policy and Finance.
Broker trade-offs between global consistency and local market needs, and build alignment on priority projects, launches and product tests.
Represent the team in senior forums, and mentor and raise the bar for others on the team through your example and feedback.

title: Program Manager, Global Retail Demo Operations, Retail Experience
location: Seattle, Washington, USA
description:
The Program Manager, Global Retail Demo Operations owns the end-to-end lifecycle of the demo devices that bring Amazon Devices to life in physical retail: Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, Alexa Tablet, Ring, and Blink. From the first demand signal at NPI through factory demo conversion, delivery to fixture vendors and stores, and sustaining replacement, this role makes sure the right device, in the right configuration, with the right content, lands in the right place on time, in every region where we sell.
This is a builder role. Today much of demo planning runs on spreadsheets, email threads, and individual follow-up. You will replace that with scalable mechanisms: a single global intake and ordering system, factory-level conversion at scale, documented approval gates, and dashboards that let stakeholders see status without asking. You will look across North America, Europe, Japan, Australia, and emerging markets and find where we can standardize, automate, and remove cost.
Based in Seattle, you are the single point of contact for demo orders from Channel Marketing teams worldwide, and you partner withNPI program and operations teams, Demand Planning, Trade Compliance, Legal/Contracts, Demo Software and Content teams, factories, and a global network of fixture vendors. You will own outcomes that are measured in launch readiness, order accuracy, and cost per unit.
Key job responsibilities
Global Demo Order Management
Own the global demo order process. Channel Marketing teammates in every region (North America, Europe, Japan, and other markets) submit their demo needs to you, and you run those orders from intake to delivery. Set the intake standard and calendar, validate each request against the fixture footprint, repair-and-maintenance buffers, and push back when quantities, timing, or configurations don't add up. Run the confidence progression (low → medium → high) against each program's NPI schedule, lock ASIN-level demand (demo SKU vs. fresh lot), and place final orders with the factory. Keep every Channel Marketer informed through one source of truth showing each order's status, ship date, tracking, and destination, so they never have to chase it.
Factory Demo Conversions
Lead the shift from vendor-performed demo conversion to factory conversion, a step change in cost per unit and speed to shelf. Define conversion specs per device, retailer, and region (content package, network profile, retail configuration). Bring North America to factory conversion for new launches, then extend the model to every region, with a clear migration plan for fixture vendors and stakeholders.
Launch Readiness & NPI Demo Last Mile
Run the weekly Demo Launch Readiness rhythm across product lines: demo experience readiness, content status, software flags, factory build and conversion status, and arrival at fixture vendors. Tie every program's announce date, street date, vendor disclosure window, and fixture in-store date into one plan, and call out risks early enough to change the outcome.
Demo Content, Configuration & Approval Gates
Own the gate before any mass conversion or deployment. Validate that demo content is live and correct in the right demo administration orgs, generate device-specific demo builds with the software team, and maintain default demo configurations for new launches. Run a documented first-article approval (proof of conversion → sign-off → release to mass production) with a full audit trail by device, retailer, region, and content version.
Vendor NDAs, MEAs, Disclosure & Chain of Custody
Own the vendor NDA and material evaluation agreement (MEA) process end to end. Request and route agreements through Contracts and Security approvals, keep a live record of which fixture and display vendors are approved for which programs and what they may receive (pre-release devices, CAD files, product information), and enforce the timing rules that govern vendor disclosure ahead of announce. Onboard new vendors and new product lines as they come up. Track pre-release hardware by device serial number with full chain of custody, and partner with Trade Compliance on cross-border movement and customs.
Prototype, Non-Powered & Packaging Units
Signal prototype availability at each hardware cycle (EVT/DVT/PVT), own allocation and budget, and prevent shortages that block fixture development. Extend the same ordering mechanism to non-powered demo shells, dummy units, and empty retail packaging for displays
Third-Party Demo Components
Own demo power supplies, cables, and other components not supplied by the factory. Manage suppliers, long lead times, and inventory positioning so components arrive with the devices, in every region.
Global Mechanisms, Automation & Data
Design and ship the systems that make this role scale: a structured global intake with auto-populated device data and suggested quantities, automated status reporting, and integrations with roadmap, catalog/ASIN, fixture, and project-management systems. Use automation and AI tools to remove manual steps. Write the SOPs so the work does not depend on any one person, then roll them out region by region.
A day in the life
How They Deliver
• Stakeholders can check order, conversion, and shipment status themselves, without asking.
• Channel Marketing teams in every region submit demo orders through one process and get them on time, in the right quantity and configuration.
• Devices arrive at the correct vendor or store, in the correct quantity and configuration, ahead of fixture build and install dates.
• Cost per converted unit drops as conversions move to the factory, region by region.
• Every pre-release device is tracked by serial number with documented chain of custody.
• Every vendor has the NDA and MEA it needs before it receives devices or information, with no launch delayed by a missing agreement.
• No program is blocked by a prototype, component, or disclosure gap that could have been forecast.
• Weekly Demo Launch Readiness runs on time, on agenda, with clear owners and decisions.
• Write narratives, SOPs, and business reviews (MBR/QBR, PR/FAQ) that drive decisions and earn trust across teams and regions.
• Identify the next mechanism to build or automate, and land it, without being asked.
• Mentor partners and peers on demo planning, and contribute to a culture of documentation and continuous improvement.
Basic qualifications: - 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Preferred qualifications: - 3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- 3+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
- Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

title: Sr. Regulatory Technical program Manager, Direct-to-Device (D2D), Amazon Leo, Regulatory, Authorization Readiness & Compliance (ARC)
location: Arlington, Virginia, USA
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's initiative to launch a constellation of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to provide affordable, reliable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Direct-to-Device (D2D) is a groundbreaking service that will bring satellite connectivity directly to everyday mobile devices, extending coverage beyond the reach of traditional terrestrial networks. To enable this, the Regulatory team obtains licenses and approvals for space, services, ground-based infrastructure, and the spectrum required to serve customers in each country where Amazon Leo will operate. There is no globally unified regulatory licensing regime for a LEO system like Amazon Leo, and most countries lack established D2D licensing frameworks entirely.
We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to join the Authorization Readiness and Compliance (ARC) team, a sub-function within the Regulatory organization at Amazon Leo. You will own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading implementation of the D2D-specific authorization plans defined by Regulatory Licensing Leads across priority countries. You will work directly with regional Regulatory TPMs, Legal, and Regulatory Licensing Leads to drive execution across FCC, ITU, and country regulators in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions, ensuring Amazon Leo can offer commercial D2D service on day one in every priority country.
D2D is a first-of-its-kind satellite service category. ITU rules continue to evolve, and jurisdictions impose conflicting spectrum and interference requirements. You will navigate that uncertainty, exercising independent judgment to implement the authorization readiness path forward where no clear precedent exists. This role demands technical fluency in Radio Frequency (RF) spectrum allocations, interference analysis, satellite communications, and 3GPP Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) standards. You will lead the implementation of complex license conditions and, in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, translate obligations into precise engineering requirements that software and operations teams can act on. You will also design and build a licensing obligation tracking platform and automated compliance reporting pipeline to manage thousands of license conditions at scale.
Key job responsibilities
•Own the D2D authorization readiness workstream end-to-end, leading the implementation of the authorization path, tracking milestones, and driving resolution of blockers across priority countries.
•Interpret complex license conditions across FCC, ITU, and country-level regulators, and in collaboration with Regulatory subject matter experts, convert obligations into actionable engineering requirements for software and operations teams.
•Drive cross-functional coordination with engineering, infrastructure, business, and operations teams to align authorization timelines with service launch schedules.
•Influence without authority across senior stakeholders in matrixed organizations, resolving competing priorities between customer commitments, engineering constraints, and regulatory realities.
•Identify and escalate regulatory risks with clear mitigation strategies to maintain compliance and prevent operational disruptions.
•Provide senior leadership visibility on D2D authorization readiness, launch risk, and country-by-country compliance status.
•Own the regulatory stakeholder relationship with key customers and partners, delivering precise updates on D2D authorization status and maintaining trust through consistent follow-through.
•Set a course in the face of ambiguity to deliver independently, asking the right questions, clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately.
Export Control
This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.
A day in the life
You will serve as the critical link between the Regulatory team and the broader Amazon Leo organization, driving cross-functional priorities with engineering, infrastructure, and business teams, and providing senior leadership visibility into D2D authorization readiness and launch risk. A key part of this role is managing the regulatory relationship with customer and partner stakeholders who maintain high expectations for communication precision, timeline accuracy, and compliance rigor. You will translate complex, evolving regulatory positions into clear narratives, set and manage expectations across competing priorities, and maintain trust through disciplined follow-through. The right candidate will have successfully managed multi-discipline telecommunications program initiatives, possess a well-rounded technical background in satellite communications, and demonstrate excellent verbal and written communication skills.
About the team
The Regulatory team secures and safeguards Amazon Leo's access to radio frequency spectrum and satellite orbital resources around the world, addresses ground infrastructure licensing and regulatory requirements, and shapes the policies and regulatory requirements that affect our ability to deliver on business goals, enabling delivery of broadband and D2D services to Amazon Leo's customers. The organization operates through three sub-functions: (i) Shaping Policy: leads public consultations, advocacy, and rulemakings at national, regional, and international levels to secure country entry, improve licensing frameworks, enable spectrum access, and prevent undesirable compliance requirements on Amazon Leo; (ii) Securing Authorizations: obtains the licenses required across broadband and D2D services and engages regulators to resolve licensing barriers and secure spectrum access and use rights; and (iii) Executing on Obligations: establishes Lawful Intercept (LI) and Law Enforcement Response (LER) programs by jurisdiction, fulfills the spectrum and network related obligations attached to held authorizations, and demonstrates compliance with service obligations. These obligations range from absolute (e.g., LI/LER) to defensible (e.g., certifications, reporting, fees, content blocking, regulator engagement), where failure carries fines, license revocations, service disruptions, and reputational damage.
The team partners with Business, Legal, Public Policy, and Public Relations to execute the strategy, and align with Design, Engineering, Operations, Security, and Business teams to keep the Plan of Record (POR) synchronized with regulatory requirements.

description:
Millions of fans stream live sports and events on Prime Video, from the Thursday Night Football, NBA Playoffs, NASCAR, MLB, MLS, and The Emmy's, to international soccer, cricket, and tennis. When a game is on, there is no second chance: if fans can't get into the stream or it cuts out at a key moment, we lose their trust. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead the programs that keep our live events available and high quality for every fan, on every device, every time. Our live event lineup grows by double digits every year, so our systems, processes and standards need to scale just as fast to keep every event reliable for fans.
You'll own how we define, measure and improve the live event experience across our own broadcasts and the ones we deliver with partners. You'll work with engineering, product, operations and partner teams to find the weak spots in our systems before game day, drive fixes that prevent repeat issues, and make sure our metrics reflect what fans actually experience. This role suits someone who is technically curious, comfortable with ambiguity, and motivated by work that customers notice right away.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the live event availability goal from start to finish: define what "available" means for fans, set targets, and report progress to senior leadership.
- Lead cross-team programs that close gaps in how we detect and measure issues during live event. Examples include fans who can't start a stream, get kicked out early or join late.
- Drive post-incident reviews and make sure the resulting fixes are actually delivered, so the same problem doesn't happen twice.
- Set and roll out operational standards for content partners, including pre-event checks, communication during major events and change deadlines, and help partners meet them.
- Partner with engineering on readiness for high-profile events: testing, monitoring, release controls and backup plans.
- Build clear reporting and dashboards that give leaders an honest view of quality and risk.
- Write clear narratives and plans that align teams and leaders on priorities, trade-offs and investments.
- Find recurring problems in incident data and turn them into long-term programs rather than one-off fixes.
A day in the life
Your morning might start with a review of last night's NBA doubleheader: what went well, what fans experienced, and whether anything needs a deeper look. Next you could meet with engineering leads about a gap in monitoring, then join a call with a content partner to walk through pre-event requirements ahead of a cricket tournament or a NASCAR weekend. In the afternoon you might refine a proposal for next year's quality goals or prepare a leadership update. On Thursday Night Football nights or during a live awards show, you'll work closely with operations and engineering teams to make sure everyone is ready, and you'll help lead the response if something goes wrong. No two days are the same. The live calendar runs from fall football to spring playoffs to summer racing and keeps the pace energizing, and your work shows up directly in the fan experience.

location: Atlanta, Georgia, United States
description:
About Flexport:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Global Operations Specialist
Help our customers improve their global supply chains
The Opportunity:
At Flexport, we know global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global trade easier for everyone. Flexport today connects more than 10,000 clients, both consignees and shippers, across 112 countries. Our role is to help businesses of all sizes find the global trade solutions that will empower their success.
Now more than ever, customers need our support to survive and win in 2026. Their success is our success. We work back from what’s best for them to find a solution. That’s why we are building the Platform for Global trade - a strategic model combining customer centricity, supply chain expertise, advanced technology, and data analytics.
As a Global Operations Specialist, you are responsible for executing the shipment lifecycle for Ocean & Air shipments, ensuring data integrity is maintained at the highest standard, and proactively minimizing delays with urgency.
As a new team member in our North American Operations group, you'll begin by immersing yourself in our company culture and mastering world-class operations. As Flexport continues to grow, there could be opportunities for future Flexporters to become founding team members in new markets, relocate internationally, and help us expand our presence around the world. If you're interested in a fast-paced career with the potential for international experience, this opportunity could offer you unmatched growth and adventure.
You will:
Be responsible for executing the movement of ocean and air freight shipments from booking at origin to final delivery at destination.
Maintain communications with Flexport transportation and warehousing partners to facilitate the progress of shipments in transit.
Work and communicate cross-functionally within Flexport
Be a part of the frontline groups ensuring the highest standard of Flexport quality: shipments move on time and exceptions are handled appropriately.
Use metrics to spot opportunities to improve and deliver great performance in your role.
Own the data quality of our client's information by validating booked shipments, tracking client shipment status, and validating shipment schedules.
Consistently follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure that your work satisfies internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) in line with productivity goals.
You should have:
Bachelor's/Associate's degree OR 1+ year of relevant experience preferred. New graduates are encouraged to apply!
Team-centric mindset: obsessed with team outcomes, doing what it takes to deliver the team’s and their client’s expectations.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail in a high-energy, fast-paced environment.
Proficient in Google Suite/Microsoft Suite (Sheets/Excel).
Fluency in English, both written and verbal.
A "compliance first" attitude to keep our regulators happy and enthusiastic about Flexport since we operate in a heavily regulated industry.
#LI-onsite
Commitment to Equal Opportunity
At Flexport, our ability to fulfill our mission of making global commerce easy and accessible relies on having a diverse, dedicated and engaged workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, health status, marital and family status, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. Please see our Privacy Notice available at  www.flexport.com/privacy  for additional information.

Strategic Finance Partnership

Develop trusted advisor relationships with sourcing leaders by providing objective, data-driven insights and constructive challenge to business assumptions.
Support the development and execution of sourcing strategies that improve profitability, cost competitiveness, cash flow, and enterprise value creation.
Translate complex sourcing and market dynamics into actionable recommendations for Operations, Finance, and Executive Leadership.

Establish and maintain financial models used to forecast commodity, currency, and supplier cost impacts across the enterprise.

Provide financial leadership and support during supplier negotiations, contract development, and cost management initiatives.
Oversee purchase price variance analysis and value-realization tracking to ensure sourcing initiatives deliver expected results.
Direct financial evaluation of inflation mitigation, supplier productivity, and continuous improvement initiatives across the sourcing portfolio.

Monitor and communicate the financial impact of sourcing-related working capital initiatives and contractual changes.
Validate realized savings and identify risks to value achievement, ensuring financial commitments are accurately measured and reported.

description:

Use WMS tools and reporting to analyze performance and improve efficiency, service, quality, and cost.

Strong communication, leadership, and change management skills.
Advanced proficiency with ERP systems, Microsoft Office, and operational reporting tools.

APICS/ASCM CPIM or CSCP certification.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher.
Experience managing high-volume distribution center operations.
Experience within manufacturing distribution environments.

The Clinical Applications Engineer (CAE) reports to the Manager of Clinical Applications Engineering. Collaborate with peers and development engineering partners to develop and share best practices and product feedback
Stay current on company products instructions for use (IFU), best practices and technical troubleshooting, as well as relevant scientific clinical literature and new product information
Prioritize and appropriately respond to requests in a high-stress environment.

A minimum of 2 years of technical or clinical experience in healthcare
Experience navigating hospitals and supporting procedures required
Self-starter who performs well with autonomy and can be flexible in a dynamic work environment
Problem solver who can maintain composure and think critically in high pressure environments
Highly collaborative and works well in a remote team environment
Effective communication skills including oral, written and interpersonal.  Strong situational awareness
Experience working with highly complex technical systems and/or working in a critical patient care setting with physicians and support staff
Ability to seek out and process large amounts of data to translate information into actionable insights
Desire to learn and build new skills
Ability to travel up to 70%, located near a major airline/rail hub, and ability to work nights and weekends as needed
Ability to independently prioritize and manage travel logistics, and complete associated administrative tasks in a timely manner
Ability to travel on a moment’s notice and support cases across varying geographies; comfortable booking and utilizing all forms of travel

Develop a culture of accountability and operational excellence that reliably delivers launches on time.

Build on the work already done to capture the launch readiness checklists and associated activities, by adding more specific details and documenting tribal knowledge, turning it into repeatable processes that can be used by all team members.
Identify and deploy best practices from a variety of sources to continuously enhance overall business launch capability and deliver value to the regional hubs.

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Team
The Incubator within Future Forward at Intuitive is a cross-functional innovation group focused on identifying, evaluating, and developing new clinical opportunities and technology platforms. The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.
Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
Experience and Qualifications
MD or DO required; active clinical practice is valued but not required for candidates with substantial innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Must demonstrate at least one of the following experience profiles: (1) meaningful hands-on clinical practice or procedural care experience plus exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) strong venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, corporate strategy, or product strategy experience plus sufficient clinical fluency to evaluate medical needs and care pathways.
Ability to identify unmet clinical needs and convert observations into structured hypotheses, need statements, development plans, or investment theses.
Experience conducting clinician, patient, or stakeholder interviews and synthesizing voice-of-customer input into actionable product or strategy recommendations.
Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where the path forward is uncertain and evidence must be built iteratively.
Strong cross-functional influence skills and ability to collaborate with engineering, clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, product, and business stakeholders.
Ability to evaluate clinical workflows, procedure economics, adoption barriers, competitive dynamics, and strategic implications for new technology platforms.
Clear executive communication skills, including crisp written synthesis, structured presentations, and the ability to explain complex clinical concepts to non-clinical audiences.
Curiosity, ownership mindset, and enthusiasm for building new technologies that can transform care delivery and improve patient outcomes.
Biodesign or equivalent needs-based innovation training preferred; experience in venture, startups, business development, product strategy, or corporate strategy strongly preferred.
Education and Training
MD or DO required.
Surgical or interventional specialty training preferred, but not required if the candidate demonstrates strong innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Clinical practice experience, residency/fellowship training, or comparable patient-care exposure preferred for candidates coming from a primarily clinical background.
Candidates with fewer years of clinical training or limited active practice experience may be considered if they bring substantial experience in early-stage innovation, venture-backed companies, medical technology strategy, product development, business development, or Biodesign.
Biodesign, MBA, MPH, MS, fellowship, or other formal training in innovation, product development, health economics, or business strategy is a plus.

Must be available to work full-time onsite in Sunnyvale, CA
Ability to travel to clinical sites, customer locations, or conferences including international (up to 25%)
May involve standing or walking for extended periods during clinical observations or procedures
Must be able to lift up to 20 lbs occasionally (e.g., for transporting prototypes or equipment)
Ability to meet hospital credentialing and compliance requirements for clinical site access (e.g., vaccination)

Minimum 8 years of relevant experience in data and analytics architecture, data products, data warehousing, business intelligence, enterprise applications, or related disciplines.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to distill complex topics for different audiences.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Data and Analytics, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
Master's degree in a related discipline is preferred.

Experience with planning, inventory, fulfillment, execution, service operations, repair, manufacturing, or related operational processes.
Experience with SAP, o9, or comparable enterprise planning and execution platforms.
Experience with Snowflake and modern cloud data architectures.
Experience designing reusable enterprise data products and governed semantic models.
Familiarity with knowledge graphs, ontologies, or related techniques for representing business relationships and context.
Experience enabling advanced analytics, data science, machine learning, or GenAI solutions using enterprise data.
Experience designing capabilities that enable self-service analysis, investigation, and root-cause analysis.

Run an effective leadership operating cadence: staff meetings, agendas, pre-reads, decision tracking, quarterly priorities, leadership offsites, and follow-up on commitments.
Develop clear, audience-appropriate briefings, presentations, communications, and recommendations for senior HR, IT, Finance, and other stakeholders.
Support planning and prioritization by bringing visibility to commitments, capacity, headcount and budget dependencies, and trade-offs; partner with accountable functional and Finance leaders rather than assuming their ownership.
Complex Programs & Special Initiatives
Personally lead selected high-priority initiatives that span teams or lack a natural owner, from framing the problem and aligning stakeholders through execution and measurable outcomes.
Build practical plans, clarify decision rights, surface blockers with recommendations, and drive action across matrixed partners without relying on formal authority.

Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.

Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.

Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Job Description
As a Corporate Chef, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and executing the culinary strategy for both the market and key customers for Kraft Heinz’s Away From Home (AFH) business. Through strategic engagement with food professionals, category managers, and culinary team members at key accounts, you will create initiatives that drive business growth for Kraft Heinz. This Corporate Chef position focuses on working with and supporting our quick service restaurant (QSR) specialty customers focusing on Pizza, Sandwich, Coffee, and International Cuisines.

Translate global and local market food trends into relevant food concepts and recipes to optimize the Kraft Heinz product portfolio.
Partner with cross-functional teams, including Sales, Marketing, and R&D, to prioritize new product offerings and improvements aligned with business objectives.
Lead professional culinary sessions with regional and global customers to showcase new products, demonstrate product versatility, and address customer needs.
Manage and grow culinary business relationships with key accounts in specific channels.

Utilize standardized customer facing templates and other corporate resources

Conduct professional and engaging presentations with confidence, ensuring seamless execution through advance planning, organization, detailed communications, and appropriate time management.

Manage internal or external kitchens with professionalism and efficiency.

title: Manufacturing Manager
location: Garland Plant, Texas, United States of America
description:
Job Description
The Manufacturing Manager is responsible for leading manufacturing operations within a large, complex food manufacturing facility with 1,000+ employees and USDA/FDA regulatory oversight. This role provides leadership across production operations with accountability for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
The Manufacturing Manager will develop production leaders, drive Kraft Heinz Management System (KHMS) principles, improve operational performance, and build a culture of accountability, employee engagement, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
As a key member of the Plant Leadership Team, this role partners closely with EHS, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, People & Performance, Supply Chain, Planning, and other functions. The Manufacturing Manager will also assume Plant Manager responsibilities and oversee site operations when the Plant Manager is off-site.
Key Responsibilities
Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations to achieve safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, and people objectives.
Ensure compliance with GMPs, food safety requirements, Kraft Heinz standards, and applicable USDA/FDA regulations.
Drive performance across key manufacturing metrics, including OEE, attainment, yield, waste, labor efficiency, downtime, service, and cost.
Lead workforce planning and labor optimization across multiple production areas and shifts.
Champion KHMS and continuous improvement, using structured problem-solving, standard work, digital tools, and data analytics to eliminate losses and improve performance.
Partner with Planning, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, and other functions to optimize production schedules, capacity, product mix, and service.
Own manufacturing cost performance and support budgeting, forecasting, productivity, savings, and capital initiatives.
Use KPIs and operational data to identify performance gaps, establish corrective actions, and communicate risks and opportunities to Plant Leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop production leaders while building a strong pipeline of manufacturing leadership talent.
Foster positive employee relations, accountability, and engagement within a large, union manufacturing environment.
Collaborate across functions to support plant priorities, product launches, operational improvements, and long-term manufacturing strategy.
Serve as a key member of the Plant Leadership Team and provide overall site leadership when acting on behalf of the Plant Manager.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business, Food Technology, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or a related field strongly preferred.
8–10 years of manufacturing experience preferred, with a minimum of 5 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
Experience leading large-scale, complex manufacturing operations, preferably within an organization of 1,000+ employees.
Experience in a USDA/FDA-regulated food manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
Union manufacturing experience preferred.
Proven ability to deliver results across safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, and people performance.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgets, labor, productivity, manufacturing costs, and operational performance.
Demonstrated experience with continuous improvement, structured problem-solving, operational excellence, and transformational change.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate operational data and KPIs into effective action plans.
Proven ability to coach, develop, and empower manufacturing leaders and teams.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and change-management skills across all levels of an organization.
Ability to work flexible hours, including nights and weekends, as required by plant operations.
