title: National Account Manager C&U
location: United States of America
description:
Plan and execute the activities of promotion and sales in multiple areas in a given region. Generate, plan, and follow up daily and monthly sales targets and actuals to achieve the sales targets of the region. Support and approve initiation, expenditures, and implementation of investments to meet the company's business requirements. Work in close cooperation with sales force effectiveness and market research professionals to effectively utilize the sales representatives and look for training opportunities and assignments that would enable their personal and career development. Follow up and increase the performance of each sales representative in the region by making double visits and carrying out periodical coaching. This is a first level of sales management.
Job Purpose
​​As a National Account Manager, you will be responsible for a specified channel. This role is uniquely positioned for an ambitious leader who is craving full ownership and accountability for our products and customers within the assigned Accounts. This is not a traditional sales role. We are searching for a candidate who shows a high level of ownership for their business and is adept at selling solutions and has a proven ability to win new business. We are seeking a candidate who is eager to be a leader, influencer and activator with internal and external key stakeholders from the first day on the job. ​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Serve as a key liaison between Kraft Heinz, the Sales organization, and assigned customers and partners, building strong relationships that drive profitable growth within the Non-Commercial Foodservice segment.
Develop and lead channel-specific priorities across K-12, College & University (C&U), Business & Industry (B&I), and Healthcare to deliver quarterly and annual growth goals, increase market penetration, and grow market share.
Manage and develop relationships across GPO/CMC partners, including Foodbuy/Compass, Entegra/Sodexo, Aramark/Avendra, Premier, and Vizient, while identifying opportunities to establish new Non-Commercial partnerships.
Serve as a subject matter expert within the Non-Commercial segment, using market, customer, insights, and sales data to identify opportunities, analyze performance gaps, target potential customers, and develop data-driven growth strategies.
Develop, track, analyze, and evaluate customer and channel business plans based on Kraft Heinz priorities, customer strategies, and external market factors to drive total customer profitability.
Lead Joint Business Planning with strategic and small-to-mid-tier accounts, tailoring programs to customer strategies while aligning with Kraft Heinz business objectives.
Build and manage a profitable sales pipeline, driving conversion of opportunities and identifying incremental branded opportunities with new and existing customers.
Grow assigned customer business through achievement of revenue and profitability targets, share gains, new and core item distribution, and effective management of Customer P&L and EBITDA objectives.
Develop customer selling stories and recommendations using insights, analytics, and market data to support business opportunities and influence customer decisions.
Develop and track Non-Commercial KPIs and sales metrics, regularly communicating wins, performance gaps, pipeline progress, and areas of opportunity during key sales meetings and business reviews.
Prepare and present periodic customer business reviews, effectively communicating business performance, opportunities, recommendations, and forward-looking strategies.
Lead and support contract negotiations, deal creation, customer presentations, and other commercial discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
Guide trade-spend strategy by channel, evaluate program ROI, and recommend or negotiate adjustments to maximize the effectiveness and profitability of trade investments.
Partner cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Legal, Culinary, Marketing, R&D, and other key stakeholders to develop customer programs, new SKUs, sales collateral, and solutions that support execution of business plans.
Support S&OP and forecasting processes, including demand planning and waste-mitigation efforts.
Challenge internal and external teams to think creatively, develop new solutions, and capitalize on emerging business opportunities.
Demonstrate strong financial and analytical acumen, including the ability to build business cases, evaluate ROI, interpret sales performance, and influence P&L outcomes.
Operate with an entrepreneurial, action-oriented mindset, demonstrating ownership, sound decision-making, perseverance, and the ability to solve complex business problems.
Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication, presentation, influence, and negotiation skills across both internal and external stakeholders.
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, sales, or related field preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
​Prior sales experience required with a demonstration of major account management resulting in profitable volume, customer penetration, attainment of new business and growth.
​Experience in national accounts sales, restaurant, culinary, and/or distributor industry preferred. Experience within the Education (K-12, Colleges, University) channel preferred.
​Command of business acumen and strong business intuition demonstrated by discernment that not every sales opportunity is equal and a track record of securing profitable volume and walking away from less profitable deals.
​Strong analytical skills demonstrated by previous experience utilizing systems for tracking and recording sales, effective business planning and data-driven strategy for maintaining current and securing new customers.
​Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, demonstrated by effective presentation, influence, and advanced negotiation skills with both internal and external stakeholders.
​Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
​Must have a valid driver’s license and meet MVR requirements.
​Overnight Travel is required, and the amount varies by territory.​
Work Environment & Schedule
This position is considered a Remote based role that can be performed from a home office with expected travel. Additionally, this role requires working a salaried, exempt schedule to best execute against customer and internal expectations.

description:

Key Responsibilities of the Role
To ensure projects are completed on time within budget or with successful attainment of objectives.
Completes specific phases or aspects of the project such as technical studies, product design, preparation of specifications and technical plans and product testing.
Design, develop, and improve internal processes and processing equipment.
Coordinates activities concerned with technical developments, scheduling, and resolving engineering design and test problems.
Controls expenditures within limitations of project budget.
Prepares interim and completion project reports.
Provide functional and technical support to the factories to minimize production and maintenance problems.
Apply engineering expertise to equipment design, problems solving, and quality improvement.

description:
Job Description:
Job Description
Changing the World, One Kibble at a Time
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for an Associate Relations (AR) Manager to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food crafter with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. From our humble beginnings, founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry. Our purpose,  To Earn Pet Lover Trust Every Day so Pets Thrive for a Lifetime ,  provides the foundation for our highest aspirations as a company.
Being a partner to the communities that surround us – and the environment that sustains us – are top priorities.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here’s the scoop - Summary
This is an exciting opportunity for a growing HR professional to make a significant contribution to the success of a highly respected global brand by supporting the organization's ability to foster a positive, respectful, and compliant workplace.
The Associate Relations (AR) Manager will be the point of contact for Associate Relations issues and inquiries within cross-functional client groups in corporate and manufacturing teams in Canada and the US. Responsibilities include building trust, credibility, and collaborative relationships with line managers and Associates.
In this role, the AR Manager will apply expertise and sound judgement when managing inquiries, mitigating risk and minimizing adverse impact on the organization by applying policies and practices and adhering to legal and regulatory requirements.
The AR Manager will resolve issues and address client needs to ensure situations are resolved fairly, objectively, and in a manner that aligns with our Champion Values, Mars Five Principles, and the Associate Concept.
The AR Manager will report to the Sr Director, Global P&O COEs & Operations and work out of our Corporate office in either Edmonton, AB, Louisville, CO or Nashville, TN on a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person.
This role will also travel occasionally to our Kitchen in Auburn, KY. The successful candidate will build strong relationships across the organization while supporting fair, consistent, and proactive Associate Relations practices.
What a typical day looks like
Conduct timely, thorough, and effective investigations relating to company policy, employment law, and other regulations.
Support the intake, tracking, and administration of Associate Relations cases, ensuring accurate, timely, and confidential documentation.
Serve as a key contact for Associates and Leaders regarding Associate Relations questions, providing guidance on policies, processes, available resources, and policy interpretation.
Coach & support the Associate Relations Coordinator with gathering information, preparing documentation, and coordinating activities related to workplace concerns and investigations.
Ensure proper case documentation is maintained to support compliance requirements and minimize organizational risk.
Escalate complex, sensitive, or high-risk Associate Relations matters to the appropriate partners for review and resolution.
Maintain and administer P&O policies within UKG HR Help, ensuring content is accurate, current, and accessible to Associates.
Build sustainable relationships with key stakeholders, including Line Managers, P&O Business Partners, Legal, site leadership, and other P&O partners.
Support Associate Relations operations through case management administration, dashboard maintenance, Workday administration, data management activities, and serving as Co-Administrator for the Workday Associate Relations module.
Analyze case data, exit interview feedback, and workplace trends to identify emerging risks and opportunities for proactive action, and prepare reports, dashboards, and insights to support decision-making and Associate Relations strategies.
Support Associate experience initiatives by coordinating exit interviews, stay interviews, culture pulse activities, and other feedback-gathering mechanisms.
Support the development and continuous improvement of Associate Relations processes, tools, policies, and case management practices.
Assist with transformation initiatives, change management activities, severance agreement coordination, and other special projects as required.
What you'll bring
5+ years of experience working in Human Resources, Employee Relations, & Employment Law preferred
Strong data and analytical skills inclusive of Excel, PowerPoint and Microsoft Co-pilot
Strong communication, written and interpersonal skills; ability to work and communicate effectively with a wide range of individuals across all levels of the organization
Ability to rapidly mobilize and manage internal and external resources to mitigate risks to the Mars business and reputation
Ability to handle and maintain confidential and sensitive information
Previous experience in CPG/Manufacturing strongly preferred
Strong conflict management skills
Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment
Strong stakeholder management
Ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, and work effectively while managing competing projects and/or demanding clients.
Motivated, energetic, goal-oriented, with a strong work ethic and positive team attitude.
A well-defined sense of diplomacy, including solid negotiation, conflict resolution, and people management skills.
Demonstrating cultural adaptability and flexing work hours given the geographical spread of responsibility.

Education: Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent level of verified military/professional experience.
Relevant Experience: 3 to 6 years of experience in logistics, supply chain, distribution, or transportation operations, demonstrating the judgment to handle unexpected operational hurdles and advise cross-functional teammates.
Leadership & Supervision: Proven background supervising and directing personnel, equipment, and resources to achieve mission-critical goals under tight deadlines.
Coordination Experience: Demonstrated track record (at least 4 to 6 months) of planning, organizing, and orchestrating the daily work assignments of team members.

Partnership & Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build strong partnerships and collaborate across production, warehousing, and carrier networks to achieve shared performance targets.

Support client- and vendor-facing communication, handling inquiries with clarity and professionalism.

Supervise, coach, and mentor night shift operational associates, fostering a high-accountability safety and continuous improvement culture.

Rating LS / LSS (Logistics Specialist / Logistics Specialist Submarine - Petty Officer): Strong match for inventory data system operations, shipping/receiving supervision, carrier liaison, receipt documentation, and supply chain accountability.
Rating CS / CSC (Culinary Specialist - Logistics & Provisioning Leads): Extensive experience in perishable goods distribution, inventory tracking systems, vendor receiving, and quality assurance.
Designator 3100 (Supply Corps Officer): Highly relevant experience directing end-to-end supply chains, freight handling, contractor oversight, and operational logistics leadership.
U.S. Air Force
AFSC 2T0X1 (Traffic Management Operations - TMO): Direct match for booking freight carriers, processing cargo documentation, monitoring contractor compliance, and managing inbound/outbound transit [source: 9, 29].
AFSC 2G0X1 (Logistics Plans): Direct alignment with distribution pipeline tracking, timeline execution, carrier coordination, and deployment/distribution logistics.
AFSC 2S0X1 (Materiel Management - Craftsman / Supervisor): Expert background in automated logistics systems, inventory accuracy, and supervising warehouse operational teams.
AFSC 21R (Logistics Readiness Officer): Demonstrated leadership directing intermodal transit, warehousing operations, contractor performance, and shift teams.
U.S. Marine Corps
MOS 3112 / 3152 (Distribution Management Specialist / Distribution Specialist): Directly translates to managing commercial freight movements, carrier dispatch, documentation, and cargo distribution networks [source: 11, 21].
MOS 0431 / 0441 (Logistics / Embarkation Specialist): Proven ability in multi-modal movement planning, load coordination, staging, and cargo manifest reconciliation [source: 3, 18].
MOS 3043 (Supply Chain and Materiel Management Specialist): High-level capability in inventory management systems, supplier coordination, and supervising material handlers.
MOS 0402 (Logistics Officer): Broad expertise managing operational supply distribution, transport planning, third-party logistics support, and leadership.

location: USA-Missouri-Kansas City
description:
Job Description:
Job: Material Handler
Segment: Mars Petcare (Greenies)
Location: North Kansas City, MO
Shift: Night Shift (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM) on a 2-2-3 Rotating Schedule (Alternating weekends off)
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. description:
Overview
As a  Critical Environment Technician  in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, recognizing safe versus unsafe work environment, having a hands-on understanding of how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays. Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members.  Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs maintenance tasks and repairs that can be performed with minimal oversight. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees maintenance tasks within a single discipline or area of expertise. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance with established mastery of maintaining systems of a specific discipline.
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Mid-Market Enterprise
location: San Francisco; New York City; US - Remote
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As a Mid-Market Enterprise Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. 

This is a rare opportunity to work as one of the early hires for a new segment within Applied AI Engineering, contributing real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in our SF or NYC office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. title: Associate General Counsel, Security & National Security
location: San Francisco
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Legal team works on the legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. Our Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI's people, technology, and services and supports their safe and responsible use. We partner closely with technical and operational teams to provide clear advice, navigate sensitive matters, and build practical safeguards.



About the Role

We are seeking an Associate General Counsel to advise across national security, cybersecurity, and platform abuse investigations and help build the programs and processes that support our work as OpenAI continues to scale. You will combine exceptional legal judgment with substantial in-house experience, turning complex requirements into effective day-to-day operations.



You will own a varied portfolio, lead sensitive matters, and help teams move from individual solutions to consistent, well-run programs. We are looking for someone who enjoys both counseling on difficult questions and doing the detailed work of implementation: defining responsibilities, securing alignment, developing useful processes, and making sure they work in practice.



You will report to the Deputy General Counsel leading Security and Public Sector Legal and work closely with Security, Product Policy, Global Affairs, and colleagues across Legal.



This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



You’ll be responsible for:

 - Advising on national security and security issues affecting AI development and deployment, including protecting sensitive technology, responding to incidents, and working with government and industry partners.

 - Leading or supporting sensitive security and internal investigations, advising on scope, evidence, investigative methods, and practical remediation in partnership with the other legal and operational leads.

 - Providing day-to-day counseling on cybersecurity, physical security, insider risk, threat intelligence, and information sharing.

 - Building and scaling legal programs, including intake and triage, repeatable business guidance, playbooks, and measures of effectiveness.

 - Counseling senior leaders through ambiguous decisions, preparing concise recommendations and executive updates, and managing outside counsel and other resources effectively.

 - Partnering with specialists in privacy, product, employment, investigations, law enforcement response, trade compliance, and public-sector matters, and taking on emerging issues across the team's portfolio.

Frontier AI is changing how organizations discover vulnerabilities, remediate risk and defend their environments. Realizing that potential at scale will take an ecosystem of partners who can put the technology to work. The Cyber Partnerships Team works to bring together providers of cybersecurity products, systems integrators, and our hyperscaler partners to accelerate deployment of this technology to enterprises around the world.

We bring together technical strategy, partner enablement, architecture expertise, and practical deployment experience, working closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and specialist cybersecurity teams.

The Supply Chain Technology team within OpenAI's Enterprise Platform & Technology organization builds the systems and data foundations that support our supply chain and partner operations. description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability.

 - Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management.

 - Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces.

 - Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing.

 - Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access.

 - Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans.

 - Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

 - You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance.

 - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

 - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

 - You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability.

 - You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation.

 - You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Health
location: San Francisco
description:
About the Team

The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity.

Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health.

Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship.

We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models.

 - Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior.

 - Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores.

 - Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians.

 - Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions.

 - Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people.

 - Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely.

 - Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem.

 - Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence.

 - Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one.

 - Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done.

 - Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product.

 - Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research.

 

If you want your work to help make medical intelligence widely accessible—and to work on some of the most important frontier problems at the intersection of AI, science, and human health—we’d love to hear from you.

Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

description:
About the Team

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.

 - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.

 - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.

 - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.

 - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities.

 - Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams.

 - Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience.

 - Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training.

 - Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation.

 - Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior.

 - Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes.

 - Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases.

 - Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models.

Nice to have:

 - Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training.

 - Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. Responsibilities Serve as the primary point of contact for owners, managing the service experience from initial appointment scheduling to vehicle handover. Listen actively to understand owner concerns, accurately document them in the repair order, and set clear expectations for the visit. Translate technical information from technicians into simple, understandable language for owners. Proactively communicate updates on vehicle status, managing timelines and ensuring a transparent process. Coordinate with the Parts and Production teams to ensure all aspects of the service visit are aligned. Prepare and explain estimates and invoices with clarity and accuracy. Ensure every owner leaves feeling cared for, confident in the work performed, and more connected to the Rivian brand. Manage internal systems to maintain impeccable records of all customer communications and repairs, ensuring all performance metrics are met or exceeded. Uphold Rivian's standards for hospitality, presentation, and process in every interaction. Act as the on-site liaison between Rivian’s centralized Service Support Operations Center and local Service Center operations. Support the launch and setup of new Service Center locations, training initiatives, and process improvements. Assist in warranty repairs and ensure compliance with state and federal automotive repair laws. Manage relationships with third-party vendors, documenting work orders and coordinating with production team to ensure seamless after-hours service completion. Proficient with laptops, computers, and modern software suites (Windows, Google Workspace, Mac, CRM systems, etc.). Exceptional organizational skills, a meticulous attention to detail, and a passion for creating order. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English. Ability to perform physical tasks such as lifting up to 50 lbs., sitting, standing, walking, and frequent use of hands for grasping tools and data entry. Physical exertion may be required to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, carrying, reaching, pushing, pulling, and lifting up to 50 lbs.). Vehicle and VIN data is accurate, governed, and usable for operational and leadership decisions. Asset movements, assignments, locations, readiness, ownership, and lifecycle status are visible across systems. Cross-functional projects have aligned scope, milestones, dependencies, decision rights, risks, and closure criteria. Engineering, Communications, Marketing, Events, Logistics, Service, Compliance, Facilities, and Real Estate are aligned to program timing and requirements. Audit and fleet-cleanup findings are converted into prioritized action plans with measurable closure. Operating processes are standardized, documented, and improved based on recurring issues and lessons learned. Capture lessons learned and convert recurring problems into process, system, or governance improvements. Lead complex or multi-site vehicle movements involving Engineering, Special Projects, Communications media loans, Commercial Fleet, Adventure Fleet, and other asset groups. Support decommissioning, reassignment, remarketing, disposal, donations/loaners, museum transfers, and other lifecycle activities through documented decision paths. Ensure movements and lifecycle decisions are reflected in the system of record and supported by appropriate evidence. Identify systemic logistics issues and recommend changes to vendors, processes, service-level expectations, or operating cadence. Coordinate ad hoc vehicle needs involving modifications, movie/media preparation, testing, content, and other specialized use cases. Ensure vehicles are routed through Jira and the appropriate fleet workflow before Commercial Asset assignment or other downstream use. Lead transition planning for vehicles entering Communications media loans and vehicles moving into Commercial Fleet after an event. Resolve ownership, priority, timing, and readiness conflicts using documented facts and escalation pathways. Provide leadership with recommendations when demand exceeds available vehicles, capacity, timing, or readiness. Jira, workflow, and operating governance Own the operating model for the applicable Jira board supporting specialized-program vehicle and asset work. Define intake requirements, workflow states, ownership, service expectations, acceptance criteria, and closure evidence. Ensure vehicle requests involving modifications, movie/media preparation, testing, or Commercial Asset assignment are traceable from request through closure. Review Jira and auto-ticket information against actual vehicle status, planned location, owner, assignee, readiness, and use case. Use the Engineering Fleet Hub as a source of truth for requests, compliance, guidelines, training, dashboards, and reporting. Establish repeatable governance for safety, audits, transportation, readiness, stakeholder responsiveness, and lifecycle controls. Identify opportunities to automate reporting, reduce duplicate entry, improve dashboards, or strengthen data controls. Audit, risk, and compliance leadership Define audit scope, sampling, evidence requirements, responsibilities, due dates, and closure standards. Lead physical audits using VIN lists, photographs, vehicle descriptions, location data, and space-status documentation. Maintain a risk-based view of missing assets, conflicting assignments, unapproved use, lost custody, readiness gaps, and compliance exposure. Escalate safety, regulatory, insurance, registration, security, or material business risks with facts, impacts, options, and recommendations. Verify that audit findings are not only corrected in the system but also resolved operationally and supported by evidence. Use data, audit evidence, stakeholder input, and operational context to distinguish urgent exceptions from process problems requiring structural correction. Integrate asset availability, readiness, logistics, budget or cost implications, safety, compliance, and lifecycle requirements into a single delivery plan. Hold workstream owners accountable to milestones and closure criteria through clear operating cadence. Replan effectively when scope, vehicle availability, timing, or program requirements change. Deliver sustainable outcomes that remain accurate after the immediate project or event is complete. High School diploma / GED
Demonstrated knowledge of mechanical operations.

Knowledge and ability to use air impact tools and other hand-held tools.
Preferred:

Standing: Most tasks are performed in a standing position with intermittent walking.

Pulling: Occasional use of electric hand truck to move parts a moderate distance.

title: Account Executive Product, Crypto/Stablecoins
location: SF, NYC
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Bridge team helps businesses build and scale stablecoin-powered financial products and global money movement through a single API. Our virtual accounts let international consumers and businesses access, store, and spend US dollars, while our payouts infrastructure helps platforms disburse funds globally.
We collaborate across product, compliance, legal, and operations as we develop Stripe Crypto’s go-to-market approach and build a durable sales culture. Our team has built financial infrastructure at Coinbase, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, and Airbnb, and we’re focused on making stablecoins a practical foundation for global payments.
What you’ll do
As an Account Executive (New Business), you’ll help grow Bridge by turning qualified demand and outbound prospecting into successful customer relationships. You’ll own the commercial journey from first conversation through launch, translating business and technical needs into practical solutions and working with internal partners to deliver strong outcomes. You’ll also use data and field insights to improve how the team sells and how Stripe Crypto scales.
Responsibilities
Close qualified inbound leads and develop outbound opportunities through networking, cold calling, and lead follow-up
Lead discovery conversations to understand prospects’ business needs and identify relevant Bridge solutions
Manage the full sales cycle, from identifying opportunities through negotiation and close, and partner with customers and internal teams to get them live
Build and maintain client relationships that support satisfaction, repeat business, and account growth
Meet or exceed monthly, quarterly, and annual sales targets while providing detailed and accurate sales forecasts
Collaborate with product, risk, operations, and other internal teams to deliver effective solutions for clients
Lead and contribute to team projects that develop and refine the sales process and help shape the Bridge and Stripe sales culture
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
3-8 years of sales experience managing the full sales cycle for new accounts at a high-growth payments, financial technology, crypto, or technology company
A track record of exceeding sales quotas, closing net-new and upsell opportunities, and managing complex pricing or commercial negotiations
Experience using data to prioritize accounts, build business cases, and track outcomes, including familiarity with customer relationship management tools, Excel, and basic SQL, or demonstrated comfort with comparable data tools and analysis
Ability to understand technical product requirements, explain solutions across multiple technology products, and work with product, risk, and operations teams to deliver customer outcomes
Strong written and verbal communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to prioritize a high-volume territory and work persistently through ambiguity in a fast-paced environment
Enterprise AEs must be in their current role for a minimum of 24 months at the time of application.
Product Sales AE’s must be in their current role for a minimum of 24 months at the time of application.
Velocity AEs must be in their current role for a minimum of 18 months at the time of application.
Preferred qualifications
Experience managing a large book of accounts or a high-velocity sales motion
In-office Expectations
This is an in-office role. Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.
